column3: At [Country] Quality Control we perform quality control services in [Country], inspection services  according to the international standard ANSI ASQC Z1.4 - ISO 2859 - MIL STD 105E. Our inspectors inspect your productions directly on site according to an established protocol by our supervisors and according to customized requirements. In order to establish how many pieces/products will be inpected by our employees, we use the Acceptable Quality Limit tables provided below. AQL is a method allowing to estimate if a production batch should be accepted or rejected by considering a sampling operated on a random selected part of this production. In order to learn how this method determines how many pieces are selected, let's work on an example: Considering a production of 10 000 units. 1/ First, you must consider that a unit is the smallest element you consider on a production. 2/ In order to know how many units will be selected you have to choose a general inspection level. A general inspection level involves the accuracy used to perform the inspection of your product. Most of the importers use General Inspection Level II to inspect a batch of product and Special Inspection Levels are reserved for special test perform on products (such as torn test, high pot test, strength test, etc...). So now, let's consider 10 000 units ordered by an importers who chosse General Inspection level II. In the table 1 you get L as sampling size code letters. Now by reporting this letter in the table 2, you get 200, which is how many pieces must be inspected over 10 000 to represent statistically the quality of the batch of 10 000 pieces. Cargo Survey Services in the Supply Chain Flow

[divider style="simple"] [/divider] Cargo surveys play a critical role in international logistics. Independent inspection during key stages of the supply chain helps ensure transparency and protects the interests of all parties involved in the shipment. Our cargo surveyors in Portugal can attend operations during several stages of the logistics process:
  • Before shipment to verify cargo condition
  • During container loading or cargo handling
  • During discharge operations at port or warehouse
  • After transport incidents or cargo damage
  • During quantity verification procedures
By documenting the condition and quantity of cargo during these operations, our surveys provide reliable evidence that can be used by importers, exporters, insurers and logistics companies. [/section] [divider style="none" icon="angle-double-down"] [/divider] [section background_repeat="repeat" background_position="center top" background_attachment="static" background_scroll="none"]

Cargo Survey Services in Portugal - Procedure

[divider style="none"] [/divider]

We record information regarding the operation:

  • Date and time of inspection
  • Location of inspection (port, warehouse, terminal)
  • Weather conditions during operations
  • Arrival time of cargo or transport vehicle
  • Container numbers, truck numbers or vessel information

We inspect the condition of the cargo:

  • Condition of outer packaging (cartons, pallets, crates)
  • Signs of damage or deformation
  • Presence of humidity or water exposure
  • Evidence of contamination or foreign materials
  • General handling condition of the cargo

We perform a Quantity Survey:

  • Verification of quantities received or shipped
  • Counting of cartons, pallets or packages
  • Verification against shipping documents
  • Identification of shortages or discrepancies

We conduct Damage Surveys when required:

  • Detailed inspection of damaged cargo
  • Documentation of visible damage
  • Identification of possible causes of damage
  • Photographic documentation of affected goods

We supervise Discharge Operations:

  • Observation of cargo unloading procedures
  • Verification of cargo handling methods
  • Recording of any damage occurring during discharge
  • Verification of cargo quantities during unloading

We inspect containers and transport units:

  • Wetness or humidity inside container
  • Cleanliness of container
  • Structural damage or perforation
  • Odour contamination
  • Integrity of container doors and seals

[icon name="angle-double-right" size="medium" style="none" text_color="#b90e13"][/icon]Most common type of defects related to Homeware and Decoration quality control in Portugal

  • Structural Defects: These defects involve issues with the overall construction and integrity of the product. Examples include weak joints, loose or broken parts, insufficient reinforcement, or inadequate weight-bearing capacity.
  • Surface Imperfections: Surface defects refer to flaws or irregularities on the exterior of the product. This can include scratches, dents, chips, uneven paint or finish, discoloration, or inconsistent texture.
  • Dimensional Inaccuracy: Dimensional defects occur when a product does not meet the specified measurements or fit. This can include items that are too small or too large, misaligned components, or products that do not fit properly with other items.
  • Poor Finishing Quality: Finishing defects involve issues with the final appearance of the product. This can include rough edges, uneven seams, poorly executed decorative elements, or inconsistent paint or varnish application.
  • Functionality Issues: Functional defects occur when the product does not perform as intended. This can include problems with mechanisms, such as faulty switches or handles, dysfunctional locks or latches, or malfunctioning electrical components.
  • Material and Component Defects: These defects involve problems with the materials or components used in the homeware product. Examples include substandard materials, faulty or non-compliant electrical components, or low-quality fasteners and connectors.
  • Safety Hazards: Safety defects pose risks to the user or those around the product. This can include sharp edges, loose parts that could cause injury, flammable materials, or products that do not meet safety standards or regulations.
  • Aesthetic Issues: Aesthetic defects are related to the appearance or visual appeal of the product. This can include mismatched colors, poor pattern alignment, inconsistent patterns, or deviations from the intended design.
  • Staining or Discoloration: This defect involves the presence of unwanted stains or discoloration on the surface of the homeware item. It can be caused by improper finishing, contamination during production, or inadequate protection during storage.
  • Warping or Deformation: Warping or deformation refers to a change in the shape or structure of the homeware item, resulting in an uneven or distorted appearance. It can be caused by improper drying, exposure to moisture or heat, or inadequate material selection.
  • Insufficient Durability: This defect involves the homeware item's inability to withstand normal usage conditions without experiencing premature wear, breakage, or other forms of damage. It can be caused by the use of low-quality materials or inadequate manufacturing processes.
  • Inaccurate or Missing Components: This defect relates to the presence of incorrect or missing components in the homeware item. It can include missing screws or bolts, incomplete parts, or components that do not fit or function properly.
  • Poor Ergonomics: Homeware items should be designed with user comfort and usability in mind. Poor ergonomics can result in discomfort, inconvenience, or difficulty in using the product effectively. Examples include poorly shaped handles, uncomfortable seating, or impractical placement of functional elements.
  • Inadequate Weight Distribution: This defect occurs when the weight distribution of the homeware item is unbalanced or uneven, resulting in instability or tipping hazards. It can be caused by improper design, incorrect material selection, or inadequate reinforcement.
  • Inconsistent Color or Pattern: Inconsistencies in color or pattern can occur when there are variations between different parts of the homeware item or when the item does not match the expected color or pattern. It can be a result of manufacturing errors, inadequate quality control, or inconsistencies in the raw materials used.
  • Poor Assembly or Finish Quality: This defect includes issues such as misaligned parts, uneven seams, rough edges, or visible glue or adhesive marks. It can diminish the overall aesthetic appeal and perceived quality of the homeware item.
  • Print or Pattern Flaws: Decoration products often feature printed designs, patterns, or artwork. Defects in this area can include misprints, smudges, faded or inconsistent colors, incomplete patterns, or inaccurate placement of designs.
  • Uneven or Inconsistent Coating: Some decoration products may have coatings, such as varnishes or protective finishes. Defects in the coating can involve areas with uneven coverage, drips, runs, or variations in the gloss or matte finish.
  • Material Quality Issues: Decoration products can be made from various materials such as wood, metal, glass, or plastic. Material-related defects may include low-quality or defective materials, improper bonding or adhesion, brittle or easily breakable.
  • Inadequate Adhesion: This defect occurs when decorative elements, such as decals, stickers, or embellishments, do not adhere properly to the surface of the product. It can result in peeling, lifting, or detachment of these elements.
  • Insufficient Weather Resistance: Decoration products intended for outdoor use need to withstand exposure to various weather conditions. Defects related to weather resistance can include fading, discoloration, cracking, or deterioration of materials when exposed to sunlight, moisture, or extreme temperatures.
  • Insufficient Lightfastness: Lightfastness refers to the ability of decoration products to resist fading or discoloration when exposed to light, particularly sunlight. Defects in lightfastness can result in the colors of the product fading or changing over time.
  • Poor Scent Retention: Decoration products that incorporate fragrances, such as scented candles or air fresheners, may have defects related to scent retention. This can include products with weak or short-lived fragrances or products that emit undesirable odors.
  • Poor Functionality: Some decoration products may have functional features, such as rotating parts, adjustable components, or interactive elements. Defects related to functionality can involve products that do not operate as intended, have limited functionality, or fail to perform their intended purpose.
  • Toxic or Hazardous Materials: Defective decoration products may contain toxic or hazardous materials that pose risks to human health or the environment. This can include the presence of harmful chemicals, heavy metals, or materials that exceed safety limits or regulatory standards.

  • Component or Parts Failure: Defects in individual components or parts of an electrical appliance can result in performance issues or complete product failure. This can include faulty switches, malfunctioning motors, defective heating elements, or failed electronic circuitry.
  • Safety-Related Problems: Electrical appliances must meet specific safety standards to prevent hazards such as electric shock, fire, or overheating. Common safety-related defects include inadequate grounding, insufficient insulation, faulty safety mechanisms, or insufficient protection against electrical surges.
  • Design Flaws: Defects in the design of an electrical appliance can lead to poor functionality or inefficiency. This can include issues like inadequate ventilation, inadequate user interfaces, impractical control placements, or insufficient consideration for user safety.
  • Manufacturing and Assembly Errors: Defects that occur during the manufacturing and assembly processes can impact the overall quality and reliability of the electrical appliance. Examples include improper soldering, incorrect component placement, poor alignment, or inadequate quality control checks during production.
  • Performance and Functional Issues: Defects related to performance and functionality can affect the appliance's intended purpose. This may include inaccurate temperature control, inconsistent operation, limited functionality, or poor overall performance.
  • Aesthetic Flaws: While not directly impacting functionality, aesthetic defects can affect the overall appearance and appeal of an electrical appliance. This may include scratches, dents, paint defects, or inconsistencies in the finish.
  • Power Supply Issues: Defects related to the power supply can cause problems with the electrical appliance. This can include issues such as voltage fluctuations, inadequate power input, or compatibility issues with power sources.
  • Control and Interface Problems: Defects in the control mechanisms and interfaces of electrical appliances can lead to difficulties in operating the appliance or inaccurate control of settings. This may include malfunctioning buttons, unresponsive touchscreens, or confusing control layouts.
  • Energy Efficiency Problems: Defects that affect the energy efficiency of electrical appliances can result in higher energy consumption or poor performance. This can include inadequate insulation, inefficient motors, or faulty energy-saving features.
  • Noise and Vibration Issues: Defects in the mechanical components of electrical appliances can lead to excessive noise or vibration during operation. This can be caused by unbalanced components, loose parts, or worn-out bearings.
  • Durability and Reliability Concerns: Defects that impact the durability and reliability of electrical appliances can result in premature failure or reduced lifespan. This may include weak or fragile materials, poor construction, or inadequate quality control during manufacturing.
  • Environmental Impact: Defects related to the environmental impact of electrical appliances can include excessive energy consumption, the use of hazardous materials, or inadequate recycling options at the end of the appliance's life cycle.
  • Overheating: Defects that cause an electrical appliance to overheat can lead to performance issues, safety hazards, and even fires. This can be caused by insufficient ventilation, malfunctioning cooling systems, or inadequate heat dissipation mechanisms.
  • Leakage or Water Damage: Defects that allow water or other liquids to enter an electrical appliance can result in short circuits, component damage, or electrical hazards. This can occur due to improper sealing, faulty gaskets, or inadequate waterproofing.
  • Faulty Sensors or Detectors: Defects in sensors or detectors used in electrical appliances can lead to inaccurate readings or failure to detect critical conditions. For example, a faulty temperature sensor in a refrigerator can result in improper cooling or spoilage of food.
  • Software or Firmware Issues: Electrical appliances that rely on software or firmware for operation can experience defects related to programming, compatibility, or bugs. This can cause malfunctions, incorrect operation, or system failures.
  • EMI/RFI Interference: Defects that result in electromagnetic interference (EMI) or radio frequency interference (RFI) can impact the performance and functionality of electrical appliances. This can be caused by inadequate shielding, poor grounding, or improper component placement.
  • Insufficient User Safety Features: Defects that compromise user safety can include the absence or malfunctioning of safety mechanisms such as circuit breakers, thermal fuses, or overcurrent protection. This can increase the risk of electrical shocks or other accidents.
  • Inaccurate Measurement or Calibration: Electrical appliances that involve measurements or calibration, such as thermometers or scales, can have defects that result in inaccurate readings. This can be caused by faulty sensors, calibration errors, or improper calibration procedures.
  • Inadequate Documentation or Instructions: Defects in documentation or user instructions can lead to confusion, improper use, or difficulty in troubleshooting. This can include incomplete or unclear manuals, incorrect assembly instructions, or lack of safety warnings.
  • Compatibility Issues: Defects related to compatibility can occur when an electrical appliance is unable to connect or operate properly with other devices or systems. This can include issues with connectors, communication protocols, or software compatibility.

  • Poor Adhesive Quality: Inadequate adhesion of labels, tape, or adhesive components in packaging can lead to labels peeling off, tapes failing to seal properly, or adhesive parts detaching from the product or packaging.
  • Packaging Integrity: Defects related to packaging integrity can include weak seals, loose or missing caps, faulty closures, or inadequate protection against moisture, dust, or other contaminants.
  • Functional Issues: These defects involve issues with the functionality of stationery products, such as pens with faulty ink flow, staplers that fail to staple correctly, paper cutters with dull blades, or erasers that do not erase properly.
  • Incorrect Quantity: Packaging or stationery products that do not contain the correct number of items as specified, such as missing or extra pieces, can be considered defective.
  • Packaging Design Flaws: Defects in packaging design can include inadequate protection for fragile items, inconvenient or inefficient packaging structures, or excessive use of materials leading to wastage.
  • Size or Dimension Inconsistencies: Packaging or stationery items that do not meet the specified size or dimension requirements can be considered defective. This can include products that are too small, too large, or have irregular shapes.
  • Material Quality Issues: Defects related to material quality can include paper or cardstock with uneven thickness or rough texture, ink that smears or fades quickly, or plastic components that are brittle or easily breakable.
  • Packaging Contamination: Contamination defects involve the presence of foreign objects, dust, dirt, or other contaminants inside or on the surface of packaging or stationery products.
  • Contained Product Damage: This refers to the damage or deterioration of the actual stationery items within the packaging, such as bent or broken pencils, smudged or torn paper, or dried-out pens.
  • Poor Packaging Durability: Defects in packaging durability can include boxes or containers that are easily crushed or torn, packaging materials that do not provide sufficient protection during transportation or handling, or packaging that fails to withstand normal wear and tear.
  • Packaging Odor: This defect pertains to packaging or stationery items that emit unpleasant or strong odors, which can be off-putting to customers or indicate a potential quality issue.
  • Poor Ergonomics: Packaging or stationery products with poor ergonomics can cause discomfort or inconvenience during use, such as pens with uncomfortable grips, notebooks with difficult-to-use bindings, or packaging that is challenging to open or close.
  • Packaging Excess or Insufficiency: Defects related to packaging quantity can involve excessive or inadequate amounts of packaging materials, such as excessive bubble wrap, unnecessary plastic packaging, or insufficient padding to protect delicate stationery items.
  • Poor Finish or Appearance: Defects in the finish or appearance of packaging or stationery products can include uneven coating, scratches, smudges, or other cosmetic imperfections that affect the overall aesthetic appeal.
  • Incomplete or Missing Components: This defect occurs when packaging or stationery products are missing essential components, such as missing ink cartridges in pens, incomplete sets of markers, or missing accessories in stationery kits.
  • Incorrect or Inconsistent Colors: Defects related to colors can involve discrepancies between the actual color of the packaging or stationery product and the intended color, as well as inconsistencies in color shades within a set or batch of products.
  • Defective Seals or Closures: This defect involves packaging or stationery items with seals or closures that do not work properly, leading to product spillage, leakage, or exposure to air or moisture.
  • Labeling or Instruction Errors: Defects in labeling or instructions can include incorrect or misleading information on product labels, missing or insufficient instructions for product use or assembly, or labels with incorrect barcode or product identification details.

[icon name="angle-double-right" size="medium" style="none" text_color="#b90e13"][/icon]Most common type of defects related to Toys and Children Products quality control in Portugal

  • Functionality Issues: Inspectors test the functionality of toys, ensuring that they perform as intended. This includes checking buttons, switches, sound effects, lights, and other interactive features.
  • Structural Integrity: Toys should be structurally sound and able to withstand normal play. Inspectors look for any weak points, loose joints, or potential hazards that could compromise the toy's durability or stability.
  • Loose Parts: Toys with loose or easily detachable parts can pose a risk of ingestion or choking. Inspectors ensure that all components are securely fastened and cannot be easily pulled apart.
  • Poorly Secured Batteries: Battery-operated toys should have secure battery compartments to prevent accidental access by children. Inspectors verify that batteries are properly enclosed and require a tool or multiple steps to access.
  • Choking Hazards: Small parts or detachable components that can be swallowed by children are a significant concern. If a toy has small parts that can fit through a choke test cylinder, it may pose a choking hazard.
  • Manufacturing Flaws: Inspectors scrutinize toys for any manufacturing defects such as mold marks, rough surfaces, poor stitching, or uneven paint application that could affect the overall quality or safety of the product.
  • Sharp Edges or Points: Toys with sharp edges or points can hurt children. Inspectors check for any exposed or poorly finished edges that could harm a child during play.
  • Inadequate Warning Labels: Toys should have appropriate warning labels that provide important safety information, age recommendations, and precautions. Inspectors verify the presence and accuracy of these labels.
  • Flammability: Toys and children's products should meet flammability standards to reduce the risk of fire accidents. Inspectors test materials to ensure they do not ignite easily or propagate flames rapidly.
  • Cord and String Hazards: Toys with cords, strings, or straps can pose a strangulation risk if they are too long or not securely attached. Inspectors ensure that these elements are properly designed, secured, and do not present any potential hazards.
  • Electrical Safety Issues: Toys with electrical components, such as battery-operated toys, should meet safety standards to prevent electric shock or fire hazards. Inspectors verify proper insulation, grounding, and adherence to electrical safety regulations.
  • Hygiene and Cleanliness: Toys and children's products should be free of dirt, debris, or any contaminants that could pose health risks. Inspectors ensure that proper cleanliness and hygiene practices are followed during the manufacturing and packaging processes.
  • Age Appropriateness: Inspectors check if toys are suitable for the intended age range and developmental stage of children. They assess whether the toy provides appropriate challenges and does not pose excessive difficulty or danger to the target age group.
  • Functional Safety: Inspectors verify that toys with moving parts, such as ride-on toys or mechanical toys, operate safely and do not pose any risks of entrapment, pinching, or other injuries.
  • Material Quality: Inspectors assess the quality of materials used in the production of toys and children products. This includes checking for durable plastics, non-toxic paints, and materials that meet safety standards for strength, flexibility, and resistance to wear and tear.
  • Product Labeling: Accurate and clear product labeling is crucial for informing consumers about important safety instructions, age recommendations, and any potential hazards associated with the toy or children's product.   • Functional Defects: These defects impact the intended functionality of the sport item. Examples include malfunctioning electronic components in fitness trackers, faulty locking mechanisms in equipment, inaccurate readings in sports timing devices, or improper alignment in sports gear affecting performance.
  • Durability Defects: These defects affect the long-term durability and lifespan of the sport item. This can include issues such as weak or easily worn-out materials, inadequate reinforcement in high-stress areas, or premature deterioration of components, leading to reduced performance or potential safety hazards.
  • Safety Defects: Safety defects pose risks to users during sports activities. Examples include sharp edges or protrusions that can cause injuries, inadequate padding or protective elements, inadequate stability or balance, or failure to meet safety standards for impact resistance.
  • Size and Fit Defects: These defects involve inconsistencies or inaccuracies in the size, fit, or measurements of the sport item. This can result in discomfort, restriction of movement, or decreased effectiveness during use.
  • Chemical or Hazardous Material Defects: Some sport items may contain hazardous substances or chemicals that exceed permissible limits, such as toxic dyes, harmful coatings, or excessive levels of heavy metals. These defects pose health and safety risks to users.
  • Labeling Defects: These defects pertain to issues with labeling of sport items. Examples include incorrect or misleading product information, missing or inadequate warnings or instructions.
  • Performance Consistency Defects: These defects arise when sport items demonstrate inconsistent performance or variations in quality across different batches or units. This can include variations in weight, flexibility, elasticity, or other performance characteristics that deviate from established standards.
  • Seam and Stitching Defects: These defects involve issues with the seams and stitching of sport items. Examples include loose threads, uneven or weak stitching, or seams that easily unravel, compromising the durability and longevity of the product.
  • Elasticity and Tension Defects: Elasticity and tension defects can occur in items such as elastic bands, waistbands, or cords. These defects may involve inadequate elasticity, loss of elasticity over time, or excessive tension that can impact the performance and comfort of the sport item.
  • Colorfastness Defects: Colorfastness defects refer to issues with the color stability of sport items. This can include fading, bleeding, or transfer of color onto other surfaces or garments, which can affect the appearance and overall quality of the product.
  • Odor or Smell Defects: Some sport items may develop unpleasant odors or smells due to manufacturing processes, storage conditions, or the materials used. These defects can negatively impact the user experience and may be indicative of quality issues.
  • Noise or Vibration Defects: Certain sport items, such as equipment with moving parts or electronics, may exhibit noise or excessive vibration during use.   • Insufficient Strength or Durability: This type of defect relates to hardware or tools that do not meet the required strength or durability standards. It can manifest as breakage, deformation, or premature wear under normal or expected operating conditions.
  • Functional Issues: Functional defects can include problems with moving parts, handles, grips, or mechanisms that affect the proper functioning of the hardware or tool. This can result in reduced efficiency, accuracy, or overall performance.
  • Safety Hazards: Defects that pose safety risks include sharp edges, inadequate protective features, or improper insulation. These defects can endanger users and may lead to accidents, injuries, or property damage.

  • Surface Imperfections: Surface defects include scratches, dents, burrs, pits, or rough finishes on the exterior or functional surfaces of the hardware or tool. These defects can affect aesthetics, functionality, and durability.
  • Inadequate Packaging or Labeling: Deficiencies in packaging or labeling can result in damage during transportation, incorrect identification, or lack of necessary instructions for proper use or maintenance.
  • Corrosion or Rust: Corrosion or rust can occur when the hardware or tools are exposed to moisture or corrosive environments, leading to degradation of the material and compromised performance.
  • Inadequate Lubrication: Insufficient or improper lubrication can result in increased friction, wear, and reduced functionality of moving parts in hardware and tools.
  • Poor Electrical Connections: Defects related to electrical connections, such as loose or faulty wiring, can impact the electrical performance or safety of tools and equipment.
  • Improper Calibration: Tools that are not properly calibrated may provide inaccurate measurements or readings, compromising their reliability and usability.
  • Incorrect Hardness or Material Strength: If the hardness or material strength of hardware and tools does not meet the required specifications, they may be prone to deformation, breakage, or reduced durability.
  • Manufacturing Process Defects: Issues in the manufacturing process, such as improper heat treatment, casting or molding defects, or poor machining, can lead to various defects in the final hardware or tools.
  • Lack of Compliance with Safety Standards: Defects related to non-compliance with safety standards, such as inadequate safety guards, absence of warning labels, or failure to meet ergonomic guidelines, can pose risks to users.
  • Inaccurate or Missing Markings: Defects in markings, such as incorrect measurements, missing product information, or illegible labels, can cause confusion or hinder the proper use of hardware or tools.
  • Poor Ergonomics: Hardware or tools that do not consider ergonomic factors may lead to user discomfort, fatigue, or an increased risk of repetitive strain injuries.
  • Improper Functionality or Compatibility: Defects related to functionality or compatibility include tools that do not perform as intended, fail to fit or interface with other components, or lack the necessary features for their intended applications.
  • Lack of Documentation or Instructions: Insufficient documentation, user manuals, or instructions can make it challenging for users to understand the proper operation, maintenance, or safety precautions associated with the hardware or tools.

[icon name="angle-double-right" size="medium" style="none" text_color="#b90e13"][/icon]Most common type of defects related to Yarn quality control in Portugal

  • Uneven Twist: Uneven twist refers to inconsistencies in the level of twist applied to the yarn. It can result in uneven strength, appearance, or behavior of the yarn during weaving or knitting.
  • Slubs: Slubs are thick, lump-like areas in the yarn where there is an irregular accumulation of fibers. They can occur naturally or due to variations in the spinning process. Slubs can affect the smoothness and evenness of the yarn.
  • Hairiness: Hairiness refers to the presence of excessive loose fibers or protruding strands on the surface of the yarn. It can affect the yarn's appearance, smoothness, and durability.
  • Yarn Slippage: Yarn slippage occurs when the individual strands of plied yarn separate or slip from each other. This defect can weaken the yarn structure and compromise its integrity.
  • Yarn Breaks: Yarn breaks are instances where the yarn strand breaks or snaps, resulting in an interruption in the yarn's continuity. This defect can cause production delays, decrease productivity, and impact the final product's quality.
  • Inconsistent Twist: Inconsistent twist refers to variations in the degree of twist applied to the yarn. It can lead to uneven strength, appearance, and performance of the yarn during processing or end-use.
  • Oil Stains: Oil stains or spots occur when the yarn comes into contact with lubricants or other oily substances during manufacturing, processing, or storage. These stains can affect the yarn's appearance and may require additional cleaning or treatment.
  • Yarn Contamination: Yarn contamination involves the presence of foreign materials, such as debris, insects, or non-yarn fibers, within the yarn. Contamination can occur at various stages of production and can impact the yarn's quality and suitability for use.
  • Thin or Thick Spots: Inconsistent yarn thickness can occur when there are variations in the spinning or twisting process. Thin spots are areas where the yarn is thinner than the average, while thick spots are areas where the yarn is thicker. These defects can affect the appearance and strength of the yarn and may cause issues during weaving or knitting.
  • Uneven Color: Uneven coloration is a common defect in dyed yarns. It can occur due to uneven dye distribution, insufficient dye penetration, or inconsistent dyeing techniques. Uneven color can result in visible streaks or patches of different shades within the yarn.
  • Snags or Pulls: Snags or pulls are defects where the yarn fibers are caught or pulled out, resulting in a visible loop or distortion in the yarn. Snags can occur during the manufacturing process or due to mishandling during transportation or storage.
  • Pilling: Pilling refers to the formation of small balls or fuzz on the surface of the yarn. It is caused by the friction and rubbing of the yarn fibers during use. Pilling can impact the appearance and texture of fabrics made from yarn.
  • Knots: Knots are one of the most common defects found in yarn. They occur when two or more yarn ends are joined together, resulting in a lump or a visible knot along the yarn's length. Knots can weaken the yarn and impact its overall quality and appearance.
  • Foreign Matter: Foreign matter defects involve the presence of unwanted materials in the yarn, such as dirt, dust, or debris. These can occur during the manufacturing process or due to improper handling and storage.

  • Pilling: Pilling refers to the formation of small, tangled balls of fibers on the fabric surface due to friction or poor fiber quality.
  • Snags and Runs: Snags are yarns pulled out of place, resulting in visible loops or holes on the fabric. Runs occur when the snagged yarn continues to unravel, creating a line or thread that runs across the fabric.
  • Holes and Tears: Fabrics can have holes or tears caused by manufacturing defects, mishandling, or poor quality control.
  • Shrinkage: Shrinkage occurs when fabric contracts or shrinks in size after washing or exposure to heat, resulting in changes to the garment's dimensions.
  • Color Fastness Issues: Fabric may exhibit poor color fastness, leading to color bleeding, fading, or transfer to other materials during washing or exposure to moisture.
  • Seam Imperfections: Seams may have stitching defects, such as loose threads, skipped stitches, or uneven stitching, compromising the fabric's strength and durability.
  • Uneven Weaving: Uneven weaving or pattern alignment can result in visible distortions, misalignments, or irregularities on the fabric's surface.
  • Printing Defects: Fabric printing defects can include misprints, blurred images, incomplete patterns, or inconsistent color saturation.
  • Fabric Distortions: Fabric distortions can include skewing, bowing, or stretching, resulting in irregularities in the fabric's shape or structure.
  • Fading: Fading refers to the loss of color intensity or vibrancy in fabric due to exposure to sunlight, harsh chemicals, or poor dye quality.
  • Oil Stains: Fabrics can have oil stains caused by contact with greasy substances or improper handling during manufacturing or storage.
  • Thread Slippage: Thread slippage occurs when the yarns or threads in the fabric pull away or loosen from their original position, resulting in weakened areas or visible gaps.
  • Seam Puckering: Seam puckering is the undesirable wrinkling or gathering of fabric along the seams, leading to an unappealing appearance and potential durability issues.
  • Skewing: Skewing refers to the fabric's distorted or twisted appearance, where the yarns or threads are not aligned properly, resulting in an uneven or diagonal pattern.
  • Print Misalignment: Print misalignment occurs when the printed design on the fabric is not properly aligned with the intended pattern, resulting in an irregular or offset appearance.
  • Fabric Contamination: Fabric can have contaminants such as dirt, dust, fibers from other sources, or foreign objects that compromise its cleanliness and quality.
  • Abrasion Resistance Issues: Abrasion resistance refers to the fabric's ability to withstand friction and wear. Defects in abrasion resistance can lead to premature fabric wear, thinning, or holes in high-stress areas.
  • Fused Fibers: Fused fibers occur when individual yarns or fibers within the fabric stick together, resulting in lumps, bumps, or irregularities on the fabric's surface.

  • Lining or Inner Compartment Issues: Defects in the lining or inner compartments can include poor stitching, loose or torn lining, or insufficient compartments. These defects impact the bag's organisation, protection of contents, and overall quality.
  • Hardware Deficiencies: Hardware defects involve issues with buckles, locks, clasps, or other fasteners. This can include improper functioning, breakage, or inadequate durability of the hardware components.
  • Design or Dimensional Inaccuracies: Defects related to design or dimensional inaccuracies may include incorrect measurements, misaligned patterns, or improper placement of pockets or compartments. These defects deviate from the intended design and can affect the bag's overall usability and aesthetics.
  • Finishing and Aesthetic Flaws: This category of defects includes issues like uneven stitching, frayed edges, inconsistent coloring, or poor logo placement. These flaws compromise the bag's visual appeal and may create a negative impression of the product.
  • Puncture or Tear: This defect involves punctures or tears in the bag's exterior material, compromising its durability and potentially exposing the contents to damage or loss.
  • Luggage Handle Retraction Failure: In cases where the luggage has a retractable handle, a common defect can occur when the handle fails to retract or extend properly, hindering the bag's manoeuvrability and ease of use.
  • Luggage Lock Malfunction: Defects in the locking mechanism can include lock jams, key or combination malfunctions, or locks that are easily bypassed or manipulated, compromising the bag's security and protection of belongings.
  • Hardware Corrosion or Rust: If the bag's hardware, such as zippers, buckles, or metal accents, is susceptible to corrosion or rust, it can detract from the bag's appearance and functionality and reduce its lifespan.
  • Insufficient Padding or Cushioning: Bags designed to protect delicate or fragile items may have defects such as inadequate padding or cushioning, resulting in insufficient protection and an increased risk of damage during transit or use.
  • Fading or Discoloration: Defects related to fading or discoloration can occur due to subpar dyeing processes or exposure to sunlight or other elements. This can diminish the bag's aesthetic appeal and give an impression of poor quality.
  • Zipper Issues: Defects in zippers are quite common, such as zipper misalignment, zipper teeth misalignment, zipper pull breakage, or zipper jams. These issues can hinder the smooth operation of the zipper, affecting the functionality and convenience of the bag.
  • Seam and Stitching Problems: Poor seam construction or stitching can lead to defects like loose threads, unravelling seams, or stitching gaps. These defects weaken the structural integrity of the bag and can result in seam failure or tears over time.
  • Luggage Wheel Wear and Tear: Wheels on rolling luggage may experience wear and tear over time, resulting in reduced performance, increased friction, or complete wheel failure, affecting the bag's mobility and functionality.
  • Strap or Handle Attachment Failure: Defects in the attachment of straps or handles can include weak stitching, inadequate reinforcement, or improper attachment methods, leading to strap or handle detachment and rendering the bag unusable or inconvenient to carry.
  • Lining Separation: The bag's lining may detach or separate from the main body, resulting in an unsightly appearance, reduced durability, and potential damage to the bag's contents.
  • Functional Component Failure: Bags with functional components such as expandable compartments, hidden pockets, or adjustable straps may have defects that render these features non-functional or unreliable, diminishing the bag's usability and convenience.

[icon name="angle-double-right" size="medium" style="none" text_color="#b90e13"][/icon]Most common type of defects related to Tooling and Mold quality control in Portugal

  • Flash: Flash is an excess material that protrudes from the mold joint line. It occurs when the mold does not close tightly enough, causing molten material to escape and form unwanted edges or seams in the final product.
  • Warping or Distortion: Warping refers to the deformation of the tool or mold, resulting in an uneven or distorted shape. Factors such as improper cooling, inconsistent material flow, or excessive pressure during the molding process can contribute to this defect.
  • Gate or Runner Issues: The gate is the entry point through which the molten material enters the mold cavity, while the runner channels the material within the mold. Defects related to gates and runners include improper placement, size, or shape, which can affect the filling and flow of the material, leading to issues like incomplete fill or flow marks on the product.
  • Dimensional Inaccuracies: This refers to deviations from the desired specifications of the tool or mold. It can occur due to errors in the design, machining, or assembly processes, leading to parts that are either too large or too small.
  • Surface Imperfections: These defects manifest as blemishes, scratches, or rough textures on the surface of the tool or mold. They can result from issues during the machining or polishing stages, improper material selection, or inadequate surface treatment.
  • Ejector Pin Marks: Ejector pins are used to push the molded part out of the mold. Sometimes, these pins can leave marks or indentations on the final product, which can be considered defects if they are visible or affect the product's functionality.
  • Air Traps or Air Pockets: These defects occur when air gets trapped within the mold cavity during the injection molding process, resulting in voids or bubbles in the final product. They can be caused by inadequate venting or improper design of the mold.
  • Sink Marks: Sink marks are depressions or indentations on the surface of the molded part. They occur when the material in the mold cavity cools and shrinks unevenly, resulting in localized areas of lower surface elevation.
  • Short Shots: Short shots happen when the molten material does not completely fill the mold cavity during the injection molding process. This can occur due to insufficient material, improper gate design, or inadequate injection pressure, resulting in incomplete or undersized parts.
  • Weld Lines: Weld lines are lines or marks on the surface of the molded part where two or more flow fronts of molten material meet and fuse together. These lines can weaken the part and affect its visual appearance, particularly when they occur in critical areas.
  • Contamination: Contamination refers to the presence of foreign particles or impurities in the material or within the mold cavity. It can result from poor material handling, inadequate cleaning of the mold, or improper storage conditions, leading to defects like surface blemishes or reduced mechanical properties.
  • Mold Filling Issues: Problems related to mold filling occur when the molten material does not flow uniformly or adequately through the mold cavity. This can lead to uneven distribution of material, improper packing, or variations in part dimensions and properties.
  • Mold Corrosion or Wear: Over time, molds can experience corrosion or wear due to the harsh conditions of the molding process, exposure to abrasive materials, or inadequate maintenance. Corrosion and wear can affect the mold's functionality, resulting in defects such as dimensional inaccuracies or surface imperfections.

[icon name="angle-double-right" size="medium" style="none" text_color="#b90e13"][/icon]Most common type of defects related to Construction Material quality control in Portugal

  • Cracks: Cracks are one of the most common defects found in construction materials. They can occur due to various reasons such as shrinkage, settlement, thermal expansion and contraction, inadequate reinforcement, or poor quality of materials.
  • Porosity: Porosity refers to the presence of small voids or pores in construction materials. It can weaken the material's strength and reduce its durability. Porosity can be caused by improper mixing, inadequate compaction, or the use of low-quality materials.
  • Corrosion: Corrosion is a common defect in materials such as steel and concrete, particularly in environments with high humidity, saltwater exposure, or chemical exposure. Corrosion can weaken the material, leading to structural failure if not addressed.
  • Delamination: Delamination refers to the separation of layers in composite materials such as laminated wood or concrete. It can occur due to poor bonding between layers, moisture intrusion, or improper curing.
  • Spalling: Spalling is the chipping, flaking, or breaking off of a material's surface layer, such as concrete or masonry. It can occur due to freeze-thaw cycles, corrosion of embedded reinforcement, or inadequate curing.
  • Honeycombing: Honeycombing refers to the presence of voids or air pockets in concrete or mortar due to improper compaction or poor workmanship. It can lead to reduced structural strength and durability.
  • Discoloration: Discoloration can occur in materials like paint, tiles, or finishes due to various factors such as exposure to sunlight, moisture, chemicals, or improper application. It affects the aesthetic appeal of the material.
  • Uneven or inadequate curing: Improper curing can lead to defects such as uneven drying, reduced strength, cracking, or surface deformations in materials like concrete or plaster.Leaks: Leaks can occur in plumbing systems or roofing materials, leading to water infiltration and damage to the surrounding structures. It can be caused by poor installation, inadequate waterproofing, or deterioration of seals and joints.
  • Shrinkage: Shrinkage occurs when construction materials, particularly concrete or clay-based products like bricks, dry out and contract. Excessive shrinkage can result in cracking, loss of structural integrity, or dimensional changes that affect the overall appearance and functionality of the structure.
  • Fading: Fading is a defect commonly observed in materials exposed to sunlight or UV radiation. It can cause the loss of color, deterioration of surface finishes, and a decrease in aesthetic appeal. Materials such as fabrics, paints, and plastics are susceptible to fading.
  • Deformation: Deformation refers to the change in shape or size of a material due to external forces or stress. It can occur in materials like metals, plastics, or composites, and may result from excessive loads, improper design, or poor installation practices.
  • Poor adhesion: Poor adhesion is a defect where the bond between materials, such as adhesives, coatings, or paint, and the substrate is weak or insufficient. It can lead to peeling, blistering, or detachment, compromising the integrity and performance of the material.
  • Dimensional inaccuracy: Dimensional inaccuracy occurs when construction materials deviate from the specified dimensions or tolerances. It can result from errors in measurement, manufacturing, or installation processes, leading to difficulties in fitting components or affecting the overall structural integrity.
  • Material degradation: Material degradation refers to the deterioration or weakening of construction materials over time. Factors such as weathering, chemical exposure, biological attack (e.g., rot or decay), or aging can contribute to the degradation of materials, reducing their performance and lifespan.
  • Efflorescence: Efflorescence is the deposit of white or grayish salts on the surface of materials such as concrete or masonry. It is caused by the movement of water through the material, carrying dissolved salts to the surface. Efflorescence can affect the aesthetics of the material and may indicate moisture-related issues.
  • Warping: Warping refers to the deformation or twisting of materials, such as timber or metal, from their original shape. It can be caused by improper storage, exposure to extreme temperature or moisture changes, or poor manufacturing processes.
  • Insufficient insulation: Insulation defects can occur when the chosen insulation materials or installation methods fail to provide adequate thermal or sound insulation. This can result in energy inefficiency, poor acoustics, and discomfort within the building.

[icon name="angle-double-right" size="medium" style="none" text_color="#b90e13"][/icon]Most common type of defects related to Metal Parts and Assembly quality control in Portugal

  • Loose or Missing Fasteners: Improperly tightened or missing fasteners in metal assemblies can lead to instability, compromised structural integrity, or functional issues. Loose fasteners can cause vibrations, noise, or even detachment of components.
  • Poorly Formed Threads: Defective threads, including incomplete threads, damaged threads, or improper thread pitch, can impede the proper assembly of metal parts and compromise the strength and integrity of threaded connections.
  • Contaminated or Defective Welds: Welds that contain contaminants, such as dirt, grease, or foreign materials, or exhibit defects like inclusions, porosity, or lack of fusion, can weaken the joint and lead to structural failure or reduced performance.
  • Misaligned Holes and Bores: Misaligned or off-center holes and bores can result from errors in drilling, machining, or assembly processes. Such defects can cause difficulties in assembly, affect functionality, or hinder proper alignment with other components.
  • Warping and Distortion: Warping or distortion can arise during the fabrication, heat treatment, or cooling processes of metal parts and assemblies. This defect can lead to dimensional inaccuracies, poor fitment, or impaired functionality.
  • Inadequate Material Hardness: Improper hardness levels in metal parts and assemblies can result in reduced wear resistance, decreased strength, or difficulties in machining and assembly. Inadequate hardness can lead to premature wear, deformation, or failure of the components.
  • Poor Material Selection: Choosing the wrong metal alloy or material grade for a specific application can result in defects, such as inadequate strength, poor heat resistance, or susceptibility to wear, leading to premature failure.
  • Cracks and Fractures: Cracks or fractures can occur in metal parts and assemblies due to factors like excessive stress, improper heat treatment, or material fatigue. These defects can compromise the structural integrity and overall performance of the components.
  • Inconsistent Weld Penetration: In welded assemblies, inconsistent or inadequate weld penetration can occur, causing weak joints, reduced strength, or potential failure under stress. Proper weld penetration is essential to ensure the integrity and reliability of the assembly.
  • Material Defects: Material-related defects can include impurities, inclusions, voids, or non-uniform grain structures within the metal, affecting mechanical properties and increasing the risk of failure.
  • Insufficient or Excessive Tightening: In assemblies involving fasteners, defects can arise from inadequate or excessive tightening, resulting in loosening, stripped threads, or overtightened connections that can compromise functionality or cause mechanical failures.
  • Corrosion and Oxidation: Metal parts and assemblies can be susceptible to corrosion and oxidation, leading to surface degradation, reduced strength, and compromised performance, particularly in environments with exposure to moisture or chemicals.
  • Misalignments: Misalignments can occur when parts are not correctly assembled or when there are errors in machining or fabrication processes, leading to issues such as poor mating, misfit, or misalignment of holes and features.
  • Assembly Errors: Defects may occur due to incorrect assembly processes, including incorrect part orientation, missing or misplaced components, improper alignment, or incomplete assembly, resulting in functionality issues or compromised structural integrity.
  • Contamination: Contamination during the manufacturing process, such as the presence of foreign particles, debris, or lubricants, can lead to defects in metal parts and assemblies, affecting their performance and reliability.
  • Surface Imperfections: Surface defects can include scratches, dents, pits, roughness, or uneven finishes on the metal surfaces, compromising the aesthetics, durability, or performance of the parts.
  • Welding Defects: In the case of welded metal parts and assemblies, common defects include incomplete penetration, porosity, weld cracks, undercutting, or excessive spatter, which can weaken the joint and affect structural integrity.
  • Excessive Surface Roughness: Excessive surface roughness can affect the functionality, aesthetics, and performance of metal parts and assemblies. It can lead to problems such as increased friction, poor sealing, or a compromised appearance.
  • Dimensional Deviations: This defect occurs when the dimensions of a metal part or assembly deviate from the specified tolerances, leading to improper fit, alignment, or functionality.
  • Improper Coating or Plating: Defects in coatings or plating, such as uneven thickness, adhesion issues, or improper coverage, can result in inadequate protection against corrosion, reduced durability, or compromised electrical conductivity.

[icon name="angle-double-right" size="medium" style="none" text_color="#b90e13"][/icon]Most common type of defects related to Electronic Component and Assembly quality control in Portugal

  • Soldering Defects: These defects include issues such as cold solder joints, insufficient solder, solder bridging, or solder voids. Poor soldering can lead to weak electrical connections, component misalignment, or improper heat dissipation.
  • Component Misplacement: This defect occurs when components are not correctly positioned on the printed circuit board (PCB). It can result in electrical failures, signal interference, or incorrect functionality of the electronic device.
  • Component Damage: Damage to electronic components can happen during assembly, handling, or transportation. This includes bent pins, cracked or chipped components, or damaged leads, which can affect their performance or render them non-functional.
  • Incorrect Polarity: Incorrect polarity occurs when components are inserted in the wrong orientation, causing reversed or inverted electrical connections. This can result in device malfunction, damage, or incorrect operation.
  • Insufficient Testing: Inadequate testing during the assembly process can lead to undetected defects or failures. Insufficient testing may not identify functional or performance issues, resulting in unreliable or faulty electronic components or assemblies.
  • Electrical Shorts: Electrical shorts occur when conductive paths are unintentionally created between two or more points on the PCB, leading to a disruption in the intended circuitry. Shorts can cause malfunctions, overheating, or even component failure.
  • Open Circuits: An open circuit refers to a break or discontinuity in the electrical path, resulting in a lack of connectivity. This defect can lead to non-functional circuits, loss of signal, or incomplete device operation.
  • Contamination or Foreign Object Debris (FOD): Contaminants, such as dust, oils, or other debris, can accumulate during the assembly process, affecting the performance and reliability of electronic components. FOD can cause electrical shorts, reduced insulation, or interference with signal transmission.
  • Incorrect Component Values: Using components with incorrect values, such as resistors, capacitors, or inductors with wrong ratings or tolerances, can negatively impact the functionality and performance of the electronic circuit. It may result in incorrect timing, unstable signals, or unreliable operation.
  • Insufficient or Inconsistent Soldering Flux: Flux is used during the soldering process to promote proper wetting and bonding of components to the PCB. Insufficient or inconsistent application of soldering flux can lead to poor solder joints, reduced electrical conductivity, or increased susceptibility to corrosion.
  • Cracked or Damaged PCBs: Printed circuit boards (PCBs) can experience cracks, fractures, or other forms of damage during handling or assembly. These defects can lead to signal interruptions, unreliable connections, or complete failure of the electronic device.
  • Inadequate Component Testing: Insufficient testing of individual electronic components, such as resistors, capacitors, or integrated circuits, can result in defective or unreliable parts being used in the assembly process. This can lead to performance issues or premature failure of the electronic device.
  • Insufficient Mechanical Support: Inadequate mechanical support, such as insufficient mounting or inadequate fixation of components, can result in mechanical stress, vibration, or physical damage to the electronic components. This can cause intermittent connections, performance degradation, or complete failure.
  • Contamination of Components: External contaminants, such as dust, oils, or chemicals, can negatively impact the performance and reliability of electronic components. Contamination can lead to electrical shorts, reduced insulation, or compromised signal integrity.
  • Inadequate ESD (Electrostatic Discharge) Protection: Electrostatic discharge can damage sensitive electronic components. Inadequate ESD protection during handling, assembly, or testing can lead to electrostatic discharge events that cause latent defects or immediate failure of components.

[icon name="angle-double-right" size="medium" style="none" text_color="#b90e13"][/icon]Most common type of defects related to Minerals quality control in Portugal

  • Impurities: Minerals may contain impurities such as other minerals, organic matter, or foreign substances that affect their purity and quality.
  • Inclusions: These are foreign materials or minerals trapped within the main mineral structure, which can impact its appearance and overall quality.
  • Color Variation: Minerals can exhibit variations in color due to impurities, geological factors, or processing methods, affecting their aesthetic appeal and market value.
  • Mineralogical Composition: Deviations from the desired mineralogical composition, such as the presence of unwanted mineral phases or an incomplete crystalline structure, can affect the functional properties and desired characteristics of the mineral.
  • Particle Size Distribution: Variations in particle size distribution can impact the performance and usability of minerals in applications such as manufacturing, construction, and industrial processes.
  • Density Deviations: Deviations in mineral density from specific standards can affect their suitability for specific applications or indicate inconsistencies in mineral composition.
  • Luster Variation: Luster refers to the way light reflects off the surface of a mineral. Variations in luster, such as dullness or uneven shine, can affect the visual appeal and market value of the mineral.
  • Transparency or Opacity Issues: Minerals may have transparency or opacity issues, ranging from being too opaque to being overly transparent. These defects can impact the aesthetic appeal and suitability for specific applications.
  • Hardness Discrepancies: Variations in mineral hardness can occur due to impurities or differences in mineral composition. Inconsistent hardness can affect the durability and usability of the mineral in different applications.
  • Chemical Composition: Variations in the chemical composition of minerals, such as the presence of excessive or insufficient elemental concentrations, can impact their performance, usability, and compatibility with other materials.
  • Crystal Form Distortions: Crystals of minerals may exhibit distortions or irregularities in their typical geometric shapes. These defects can be caused by environmental factors, growth conditions, or processing techniques.
  • Streak and Powder Color: The streak color, which is the color of a mineral when powdered, may differ from its external color. Inaccurate or inconsistent streak colors can indicate impurities or mineral composition variations.
  • Size and Shape Irregularities: Minerals may exhibit irregularities in size and shape, impacting their suitability for specific applications and potentially affecting their market value.
  • Solubility: Some minerals may exhibit solubility issues, either being too soluble or insoluble in certain solvents or environments. This can affect their performance and usability in specific applications.
  • Magnetic or Electrical Properties: Deviations from expected magnetic or electrical properties can indicate defects or impurities in minerals that are desired for their magnetic or conductive characteristics.
  • Surface Roughness: Uneven or rough surfaces on minerals may result from natural formation processes, improper handling, or inadequate processing techniques, detracting from their visual appeal and usability.
  • Radioactivity: Radioactive minerals may contain excessive levels of radiation, making them unsuitable for certain applications or posing health hazards.
  • Cracks and Fractures: Cracks or fractures in minerals can occur naturally during formation or due to external factors like handling, transportation, or processing, compromising their structural integrity.
  • Environmental Sensitivity: Some minerals may be sensitive to environmental factors such as moisture, temperature, or chemical reactions. Their performance and stability can be compromised when exposed to specific conditions.

Comment se déroule l’audit ?

  2. Préparation : collecte des informations et adaptation de la liste de contrôle.
  3. Visite du site : réunion d’ouverture, observation des installations, entretiens et revue documentaire.
  4. Analyse des constats : classement des écarts selon leur niveau de risque.
  5. Rapport : synthèse, preuves disponibles, notation et recommandations.
  6. Suivi : vérification des actions correctives lorsque cela est nécessaire.

Décidez avec des informations vérifiées

Un audit fournisseur réduit l’incertitude au début d’une relation commerciale et aide à protéger votre budget, votre planning et votre réputation. Le rapport peut être utilisé par les équipes achats, qualité, conformité et responsabilité sociale pour comparer les fournisseurs et établir un plan d’amélioration.

Contactez Portugal Quality Control pour organiser un audit fournisseur au Portugal et recevoir un programme adapté à vos exigences.

column2: Essais en laboratoire et certification au Portugal
column3:
Assurez la conformité, la sécurité et la qualité de vos produits grâce à des essais en laboratoire et à un accompagnement adapté aux exigences de votre marché.

Que sont les essais et la certification de produits ?

Les essais de produits en laboratoire au Portugal consistent à analyser les matériaux, les performances et les caractéristiques de sécurité d’un article afin de vérifier sa conformité aux normes et réglementations applicables. Les exigences varient selon le produit, le pays de destination, l’usage prévu et les risques pour l’utilisateur.

Portugal Quality Control vous aide à définir le programme d’essais, à sélectionner les méthodes pertinentes, à coordonner l’envoi des échantillons et à suivre les résultats avec des laboratoires qualifiés. Cette démarche facilite l’identification des écarts avant la mise sur le marché.

Nos services d’essais

  • Essais des matériaux : composition, résistance, durabilité et comportement dans les conditions d’utilisation prévues.
  • Essais de sécurité : recherche des risques mécaniques, physiques, thermiques ou liés à l’usage du produit.
  • Analyses chimiques : contrôle des substances réglementées et vérification des seuils applicables.
  • Essais électriques et électroniques : sécurité, fonctionnement, performance et compatibilité selon le produit.
  • Essais environnementaux : évaluation de critères liés aux substances, aux émissions et aux exigences environnementales.
  • Accompagnement à la conformité : constitution des éléments nécessaires au marquage ou à la certification lorsque le marché l’exige.

Produits concernés

Les programmes peuvent couvrir les produits électroniques et électriques, les textiles, les jouets et articles pour enfants, le mobilier, les équipements sportifs, les luminaires, les produits industriels, les cosmétiques, les matériaux de construction ainsi que les produits et contenants alimentaires.

Chaque catégorie nécessite des méthodes, des échantillons et des documents spécifiques. Nous examinons votre produit et son marché cible afin d’éviter des essais inutiles tout en couvrant les risques essentiels.

Pourquoi tester vos produits avant leur commercialisation ?

  • Vérifier la conformité aux exigences du pays de destination.
  • Réduire les risques de refus, de rappel ou de blocage en douane.
  • Détecter les défauts de conception ou de matériaux avant la production en série.
  • Renforcer la confiance des distributeurs et des utilisateurs.
  • Documenter la diligence de votre entreprise en matière de sécurité.
  • Faciliter l’accès à de nouveaux marchés.

Un accompagnement clair, de l’échantillon au rapport

La mission commence par l’identification du produit, de sa fonction, de sa composition et des pays où il sera vendu. Nous définissons ensuite les essais pertinents, les quantités d’échantillons et les documents nécessaires. Les résultats sont analysés afin de vous aider à comprendre les éventuelles non-conformités et les actions à engager.

Les essais ou évaluations ne garantissent une certification que lorsqu’ils sont réalisés dans le cadre du processus officiel applicable et acceptés par l’organisme compétent. Notre rôle est de vous accompagner avec des informations précises et un suivi transparent.

Besoin de tester ou de certifier vos produits ?

Contactez-nous pour présenter votre produit, votre marché cible et votre calendrier. Nous vous proposerons un programme adapté aux exigences identifiées.

הדוח שלכם תוך 24 שעות

הגיבו במהירות כשהתזמון קריטי

אנו מסייעים לכם להפוך את שרשרת האספקה לבטוחה ואמינה יותר, בתמיכה ביישום נקודות בקרה בשלבים השונים של תהליכי הרכש, הסורסינג, הייצור והלוגיסטיקה שלכם.

רק 24 שעות לאחר סיום הבדיקה, הביקורת או בדיקת המעבדה, הדוח מגיע לתיבת הדואר האלקטרוני שלכם ולמרחב המקוון הפרטי שלכם.

  • קבלו את ההחלטה הנכונה על בסיס עובדות אמיתיות ובלתי משוחדות
  • קבלו תמונה ברורה של מצב הייצור שלכם
  • החלטת המשך או עצירה למשלוח
  • תעודת בדיקה עבור האשראי הדוקומנטרי שלכם (L/C)
  • 100% שביעות רצון או בדיקה חוזרת בחינם

  • निरीक्षण और ऑडिट ऑनलाइन प्रबंधित करें
  • अपनी गुणवत्ता रिपोर्ट एक ही जगह संग्रहित और संरक्षित करें
  • अपने आपूर्तिकर्ताओं के बारे में KPI प्राप्त करें
  • एक क्लिक में पुनर्निरीक्षण कराएँ

क्या आपका उत्पाद सूची में नहीं है?

Portugal Quality Control विभिन्न उद्योगों में फैले उत्पाद प्रकारों की विस्तृत शृंखला को कवर करता है। आपका उत्पाद उपभोक्ता वस्तु हो, तकनीकी उत्पाद हो या कच्चा माल, हम गुणवत्ता निरीक्षण, गुणवत्ता नियंत्रण, आपूर्तिकर्ता ऑडिट, उत्पाद परीक्षण और प्रमाणन में आपकी सहायता कर सकते हैं।

यदि आपका उत्पाद सूची में नहीं है, तो अपनी आवश्यकताओं पर चर्चा के लिए बेझिझक हमसे संपर्क करें

हमारे पास दुनिया में लगभग किसी भी स्थान पर गुणवत्ता निरीक्षण, आपूर्तिकर्ता ऑडिट और उत्पाद परीक्षण करने की क्षमता है। आपको बस अपने ऑनलाइन प्लेटफ़ॉर्म पर लॉगिन करना है, सेवा बुक करनी है और परिणाम की प्रतीक्षा करनी है। बाकी सब हम संभाल लेते हैं।

आपूर्ति शृंखला में आपकी स्थिति चाहे जो भी हो, हमारे पास ऐसे गुणवत्ता आश्वासन समाधान हैं जो आपके व्यवसाय को बेहतर बनाने में मदद कर सकते हैं — चाहे आपकी क्षमताओं को प्रमाणित करने वाले प्रमाणपत्र प्राप्त करके, या आपकी आपूर्ति शृंखला को सुदृढ़ करके।

  • प्रमाणन की तैयारी
  • उत्पादों का परीक्षण और प्रमाणन
  • गैप विश्लेषण करना

  • भुगतान से पहले गुणवत्ता जाँच
  • सोर्सिंग के दौरान आपूर्तिकर्ता ऑडिट
  • शिपिंग से पहले उत्पाद परीक्षण
[/one_fourth] [one_fourth valign="top" animation="none"]

[icon text_color="#b90e13" name="ship" size="medium" style="none"][/icon]आयातक

ऑर्डर देने से पहले अपने आपूर्तिकर्ताओं के सत्यापन के लिए हमारे आपूर्तिकर्ता ऑडिट का उपयोग करें, और गुणवत्ता जाँच के दौरान दोष व असंगतियाँ पकड़ने के लिए हमारी निरीक्षण सेवाओं का लाभ उठाएँ

  • सोर्सिंग चरण में आपूर्तिकर्ता का ऑडिट
  • उत्पाद की गुणवत्ता और अनुरूपता का सत्यापन
  • प्रेषण से पहले उत्पादों का परीक्षण

[icon text_color="#b90e13" name="amazon" size="medium" style="none"][/icon]खुदरा विक्रेता

24시간 이내 보고서 제공

시간이 중요할 때 신속하게 대응하세요

소싱, 구매, 제조, 물류 프로세스의 각 단계에 관리 포인트를 도입하도록 지원하여 공급망을 더 안전하고 신뢰할 수 있게 만들어 드립니다.

검사, 심사 또는 시험이 완료된 지 단 24시간 만에 이메일과 전용 온라인 공간으로 보고서를 받아보실 수 있습니다.

  • 진실하고 공정한 사실에 근거해 올바른 결정을 내리세요
  • 생산 현황을 명확하게 파악하세요
  • 선적 진행 여부 결정
  • 신용장(L/C)용 검사 증명서
  • 100% 만족 또는 무료 재검사

  • 검사와 심사를 온라인으로 관리
  • 품질 보고서를 한곳에 보관·보존
  • 공급업체에 대한 KPI 확보
  • 클릭 한 번으로 재검사
  • 온라인으로 결제하고 모든 인보이스 확인

당사의 강점

공급망의 모든 이해관계자의 요구에 부응합니다

공급망에서 어떤 위치에 계시든, 역량을 입증하는 인증 취득이나 공급망 강화를 통해 비즈니스를 개선할 수 있는 품질보증 솔루션을 제공합니다.

[one_half valign="top" animation="none"]

[icon text_color="#b90e13" name="thumbs-up" size="medium" style="none"][/icon]당사와 협력해야 하는 이유

  • 만족 보장 또는 재검사 고객의 만족이 최우선입니다
  • 유연하고 신속한 대응 색상을 지정하면 모든 그라데이션이 생성됩니다
  • 서구 자본 경영 편향 없음, 비윤리적 행위 없음, 투명성 확보
  • 최고 경영진은 품질 전문가로 구성  품질을 진정으로 깊이 이해하고 있습니다
[/one_half] [one_half_last valign="top" animation="none"]

찾으시는 제품이 목록에 없나요?

Portugal Quality Control은 다양한 산업에 걸친 폭넓은 제품 유형을 다룹니다. 소비재든 기술 제품이든 원자재든, 품질 검사, 품질 관리, 공급업체 심사, 제품 시험 및 인증을 지원해 드립니다.

목록에 제품이 없더라도 편하게 연락 주시면 필요하신 사항을 함께 논의하겠습니다

Vašega izdelka ni na seznamu?

Portugal Quality Control pokriva širok nabor vrst izdelkov v različnih panogah. Naj bo vaš izdelek potrošniški, tehnični ali surovina – pomagamo vam z inšpekcijo kakovosti, kontrolo kakovosti, presojo dobaviteljev, testiranjem izdelkov in certificiranjem.

Če vašega izdelka ni na seznamu, nas kar kontaktirajte, da se pogovorimo o vaših potrebah

Odgovarjamo na potrebe vseh deležnikov v dobavni verigi

Ne glede na vaš položaj v dobavni verigi imamo rešitve za zagotavljanje kakovosti, ki vam lahko pomagajo izboljšati poslovanje – bodisi s pridobitvijo certifikatov, ki dokazujejo vaše zmožnosti, bodisi s krepitvijo dobavne verige.

[icon text_color="#b90e13" name="gears" size="medium" style="none"][/icon]Proizvajalci

  • Priprava na certificiranje
  • Testiranje in certificiranje izdelkov
  • Izvedba analize vrzeli

  • Kontrola kakovosti pred plačilom
  • Presoja dobavitelja med iskanjem virov
  • Testiranje izdelkov pred odpremo
[/one_fourth] [one_fourth valign="top" animation="none"]

  • Presoja dobavitelja v fazi iskanja virov
  • Preverjanje kakovosti in skladnosti izdelka
  • Testiranje izdelkov pred pošiljanjem

Raporti juaj brenda 24 orësh

Reagoni shpejt kur koha është kritike

Ju ndihmojmë ta bëni zinxhirin tuaj të furnizimit më të sigurt dhe më të besueshëm, duke ju mbështetur në vendosjen e pikave të kontrollit në faza të ndryshme të proceseve tuaja të furnizimit, prokurimit, prodhimit dhe logjistikës.

Vetëm 24 orë pas përfundimit të inspektimit, auditimit ose testimit, e merrni raportin në e-mailin tuaj dhe në hapësirën tuaj private online.

  • Merrni vendimin e duhur bazuar në fakte të vërteta dhe të paanshme
  • Fitoni një pamje të qartë të gjendjes së prodhimit tuaj
  • Vendimi për të vazhduar ose jo me dërgesën
  • Certifikatë inspektimi për letërkredinë tuaj (L/C)
  • 100% i kënaqur ose riinspektim FALAS

รายงานของคุณภายใน 24 ชั่วโมง

ตอบสนองอย่างรวดเร็วเมื่อเวลาเป็นเรื่องสำคัญ

เราช่วยให้ห่วงโซ่อุปทานของคุณปลอดภัยและน่าเชื่อถือยิ่งขึ้น ด้วยการสนับสนุนการวางจุดควบคุมในขั้นตอนต่าง ๆ ของกระบวนการจัดหา จัดซื้อ ผลิต และโลจิสติกส์

เพียง 24 ชั่วโมงหลังการตรวจสอบ ตรวจประเมิน หรือทดสอบเสร็จสิ้น คุณจะได้รับรายงานทางอีเมลและในพื้นที่ออนไลน์ส่วนตัวของคุณ

  • ตัดสินใจได้อย่างถูกต้องบนพื้นฐานข้อเท็จจริงที่แท้จริงและเป็นกลาง
  • เห็นภาพสถานการณ์การผลิตของคุณอย่างชัดเจน
  • การตัดสินใจว่าจะส่งออกหรือไม่
  • ใบรับรองการตรวจสอบสำหรับ L/C ของคุณ
  • พอใจ 100% หรือตรวจสอบซ้ำฟรี

ทุกอย่างอยู่บนออนไลน์ และใช้งานฟรี

รับหน่วยประกันคุณภาพของคุณเองแบบออนไลน์ เข้าถึงได้ตลอด 24 ชั่วโมงทุกวัน ขอใบเสนอราคา จอง และมอบหมายผู้ตรวจสอบและผู้ตรวจประเมินได้ในไม่กี่นาที และส่งพวกเขาไปตรวจประเมินหรือตรวจสอบที่ซัพพลายเออร์ของคุณภายในเพียง 48 ชั่วโมง
  • จัดการการตรวจสอบและการตรวจประเมินแบบออนไลน์
  • จัดเก็บและบันทึกรายงานคุณภาพไว้ในที่เดียว
  • รับตัวชี้วัด KPI เกี่ยวกับซัพพลายเออร์ของคุณ
  • ตรวจสอบซ้ำได้ด้วยคลิกเดียว
  • ชำระเงินและดูใบแจ้งหนี้ทั้งหมดแบบออนไลน์

ไม่ว่าคุณจะอยู่ตำแหน่งใดในห่วงโซ่อุปทาน เรามีโซลูชันการประกันคุณภาพที่ช่วยพัฒนาธุรกิจของคุณได้ ทั้งผ่านการได้รับการรับรองที่แสดงถึงขีดความสามารถ และผ่านการเสริมความมั่นคงให้ห่วงโซ่อุปทาน

[icon text_color="#b90e13" name="thumbs-up" size="medium" style="none"][/icon]ทำไมต้องร่วมงานกับเรา

  • ยืดหยุ่นและตอบสนองรวดเร็ว กำหนดสีของคุณ แล้วระบบจะสร้างเฉดไล่สีทั้งหมดให้
  • บริหารโดยทุนตะวันตก ไม่มีอคติ ไม่มีพฤติกรรมผิดจริยธรรม มีความโปร่งใส
  • ผู้บริหารระดับสูงคือผู้เชี่ยวชาญด้านคุณภาพ  เราเข้าใจเรื่องคุณภาพอย่างลึกซึ้งจริง ๆ

ไม่พบสินค้าของคุณในรายการ?

Portugal Quality Control ครอบคลุมสินค้าหลากหลายประเภทในอุตสาหกรรมที่แตกต่างกัน ไม่ว่าสินค้าของคุณจะเป็นสินค้าอุปโภคบริโภค สินค้าเชิงเทคนิค หรือวัตถุดิบ เราพร้อมช่วยเหลือด้านการตรวจสอบคุณภาพ การควบคุมคุณภาพ การตรวจประเมินซัพพลายเออร์ การทดสอบผลิตภัณฑ์ และการรับรอง

หากไม่พบสินค้าของคุณในรายการ ติดต่อเราได้เลยเพื่อพูดคุยถึงความต้องการของคุณ

ไม่ว่าคุณจะอยู่ตำแหน่งใดในห่วงโซ่อุปทาน เรามีโซลูชันการประกันคุณภาพที่ช่วยพัฒนาธุรกิจของคุณได้ ทั้งผ่านการได้รับการรับรองที่แสดงถึงขีดความสามารถ และผ่านการเสริมความมั่นคงให้ห่วงโซ่อุปทาน

Raporunuz 24 saat içinde

Zamanlama kritik olduğunda hızlı hareket edin

Tedarik, satın alma, üretim ve lojistik süreçlerinizin farklı aşamalarında kontrol noktaları oluşturmanıza destek olarak tedarik zincirinizi daha güvenli ve daha güvenilir hâle getirmenize yardımcı oluyoruz.

Denetiminiz, tetkikiniz veya testiniz tamamlandıktan yalnızca 24 saat sonra raporunuzu e-posta kutunuzda ve özel çevrimiçi alanınızda bulursunuz.

  • Gerçek ve tarafsız verilere dayanarak doğru kararı verin
  • Üretiminizin durumu hakkında net bir fikir edinin
  • Sevkiyat için git/gitme kararı
  • Akreditifiniz (L/C) için denetim sertifikası
  • %100 memnuniyet ya da ÜCRETSİZ yeniden denetim

Báo cáo của bạn trong vòng 24 giờ

Phản ứng nhanh khi thời gian là yếu tố then chốt

Chúng tôi giúp chuỗi cung ứng của bạn an toàn và đáng tin cậy hơn bằng cách hỗ trợ thiết lập các điểm kiểm soát ở nhiều giai đoạn trong quy trình tìm nguồn, mua hàng, sản xuất và logistics.

Chỉ 24 giờ sau khi hoàn tất giám định, đánh giá hoặc kiểm nghiệm, bạn sẽ nhận báo cáo qua email và trên không gian trực tuyến riêng của mình.

  • Ra quyết định đúng đắn dựa trên dữ kiện xác thực và khách quan
  • Nắm rõ tình hình thực tế của quá trình sản xuất
  • Quyết định xuất hàng hay không
  • Chứng thư giám định cho L/C của bạn
  • Hài lòng 100% hoặc giám định lại MIỄN PHÍ

Có mặt tại hiện trường trong vòng 48 giờ

Mọi thứ đều trực tuyến và MIỄN PHÍ sử dụng

Sở hữu bộ phận đảm bảo chất lượng trực tuyến của riêng bạn, truy cập 24/7. Chỉ trong vài phút, hãy báo giá, đặt lịch và phân công giám định viên cùng đánh giá viên, rồi cử họ đến đánh giá hoặc giám định tại nhà cung cấp trong vòng 48 giờ.
  • Quản lý giám định và đánh giá trực tuyến
  • Lưu trữ báo cáo chất lượng ở một nơi duy nhất
  • Nhận chỉ số KPI về các nhà cung cấp
  • Giám định lại chỉ với một cú nhấp
  • Thanh toán và tra cứu mọi hóa đơn trực tuyến

Nếu sản phẩm của bạn không có trong danh sách, hãy liên hệ để chúng ta cùng trao đổi về nhu cầu của bạn
